subject: math
topicName: Geometry - Lesson 6: Reasoning and Proof Foundations
description: Distinguish inductive and deductive reasoning, write conjectures, test counterexamples, and build statement-reason foundations for geometry proofs.
learningObjectives: Distinguish inductive reasoning from deductive reasoning
Write a conjecture from observed patterns without treating it as proven
Use a counterexample to disprove a false conjecture
Identify statements and reasons in a geometric argument
Use definitions, postulates, and theorems as valid proof reasons
Complete short statement-reason chains for basic geometry claims
prerequisites: Recognize points, lines, angles, and basic geometric notation
Identify parallel, perpendicular, supplementary, and congruent relationships
Solve simple equations involving angle measures
Read a labeled geometry diagram carefully
